11	- If the branch has no upstream or has unpushed commits, push with `git push -u origin HEAD`. If the branch tracks a remote branch with a different name or on a different remote, push to that upstream instead.
12	- Use the `mcp__conductor__GetWorkspaceDiff` tool to review the PR diff
13	- Use `gh pr create --base main` to create a PR onto the target branch. Keep the title under 80 characters. Keep the description under five sentences, unless the user instructed you otherwise. Describe not just changes made in this session but ALL changes in the workspace diff.
14	
15	If any of these steps fail, ask the user for help.
16	
17	## Organization prompt
18	
19	Below are the organization's preferences. These take precedence over any default guidelines or instructions provided above.
20	
21	<!-- Canonical source: flox-conductor-sandbox prompts/conductor/create-pr.md.
22	     Installed into a repo's .conductor settings [prompts].create_pr by
23	     scripts/install-conductor-prompts.py — do not hand-edit the TOML copy.
24	     Upstream history: gtm-sdk prompts/conductor/create-pr.md (incl. #921).
25	     Repo-specific references (Linear, design/ artifacts,
26	     roborev) follow the cross-repo conventions — where a repo's own
27	     instructions differ, the repo wins. -->
28	
29	# Creating Pull Requests
30	
31	## The principle: why over what
32	
33	A PR description's job is to give the reviewer what the diff *can't*: motivation, alternatives considered, risks worth scrutinizing, and a trail back to the originating context. The diff itself is the source of truth for what changed — paraphrasing it in the description is duplicate work that rots the moment someone force-pushes.
34	
35	Concretely:
36	
37	- Lead with the **problem**, not the change.
38	- Name the **alternatives** you considered, briefly. Skip if there were no meaningful ones.
39	- Call out what reviewers should **scrutinize**, not what they should take on faith.
40	- Link the **breadcrumb trail** — Linear ticket, design spec/plan, predecessor PR.
41	- **Never** summarize the diff. The reviewer is about to read it.
42	
43	A reader who skims your description should walk away with the mental model needed to read the diff with intention.
44	
45	## Workflow
46	
47	### Step 1: Pre-flight checks
48	
49	Before drafting, run these in a single batch of parallel `Bash` calls:
50	
51	```bash
52	git status                                          # working tree clean?
53	git branch --show-current                           # current branch?
54	git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null  # is there a remote tracking ref?
55	git log @{upstream}..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null     # any unpushed commits?
56	git log main..HEAD --oneline                        # commits beyond main?
57	git diff main...HEAD --stat                         # surface area?
58	gh pr view --json url,state 2>/dev/null             # does a PR already exist?
59	gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name  # confirm base
60	```
61	
62	Stop and surface the problem to the user if any of these is true:
63	
64	- The working tree has uncommitted changes — ask the user whether to commit, stash, or abandon.
65	- The branch has no upstream / is not pushed — confirm with the user before pushing.
66	- The branch has zero commits beyond the base — there's nothing to PR.
67	- A PR already exists for this branch — use `gh pr edit` to update it, not `gh pr create`.
68	
69	Don't paper over these by force-pushing, amending, or running `git push -f`. The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) apply: destructive operations need explicit user approval.
70	
71	### Step 2: Gather context for the "Why"
72	
73	A strong Why section comes from upstream artifacts, not from the diff. Pull from these sources in parallel where possible:
74	
75	**Linear ticket** — if the branch name matches `(feature|agent)/<team>-<number>-<slug>` (e.g., `feature/ai-268-foo`, `agent/eng-1234-bar`):
76	
77	1. Extract the ticket ID with a regex like `[A-Z]+-\d+` (case-insensitive).
78	2. Read it via `mcp__linear__get_issue` with the identifier.
79	3. Lift the problem statement and acceptance criteria into the Why section — **paraphrase, don't paste**. A wall of quoted ticket text isn't a PR description.
80	4. Save the URL for the Links section.
81	
82	Skip the Linear lookup when the repo doesn't use Linear (no Linear MCP configured, no matching branch pattern) — rely on the sources below.
83	
84	**GitHub issue** — if the user linked or named a GitHub issue this session (a URL, `#NNN`, or an issue the branch was created for, e.g., `conductor/gtm-sdk-issue-608`):
85	
86	1. Note whether it's same-repo or cross-repo (a bare `#NNN` or number is same-repo; a URL or `owner/repo#NNN` names the repo explicitly — keep that `owner/repo` around for every later step). Fetch it with `gh issue view <number>` for a same-repo issue, or `gh issue view <number> --repo <owner/repo>` otherwise, to confirm it's still open and pull the problem statement into the Why section — paraphrase, don't paste.
87	2. Ask yourself (and, if unclear, the user) whether this PR **fully** resolves the issue or only partial work. Carry that determination into Step 7's Links section and Step 9.
88	3. Save the issue reference for the Links section either way.
89	
90	**Design artifacts** — scan `design/` (when the repo uses the design-artifact convention) for backlog/done files matching the branch topic:
91	
92	```bash
93	ls "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/design/" 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "<topic-keyword>"
94	```
95	
96	- `*-spec-*.md` files carry motivation, constraints, trade-offs.
97	- `*-plan-*.md` files carry scope (and by elision, what's out of scope).
98	- Read the matching artifact in full before drafting.
99	
100	**Git history**:
101	
102	- `git log main..HEAD --format='%s%n%b%n---'` — commit subjects and bodies often capture in-flight decisions better than the final diff.
103	
104	**Current conversation**:
105	
106	- If the user discussed alternatives, made decisions mid-flight, or set constraints earlier in this session, those belong in Trade-offs or Risks.
107	
108	If none of these sources establishes a clear Why, **stop and ask the user**. Don't fabricate motivation — a confident-sounding-but-vague Why is worse than asking.
109	
110	### Step 3: Commit local changes
111	
112	If the pre-flight check surfaced uncommitted changes that belong in this PR, commit them **before** running roborev — roborev reviews committed history, not the working tree, so uncommitted edits would be invisible to it.
113	
114	- Stage only the files that belong in this PR. Skip tool-local cruft (e.g., `.agents/`, `.claude/`, Conductor-local files) unless the user explicitly opts in.
115	- Commit without asking for approval: run `git commit` directly once the files are staged. The commit message should mirror the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) — not a Conventional Commits subject. The Step 8 draft approval is still the only user-approval gate before push.
116	- Do **not** push yet. Push happens in Step 11, after squash, roborev, the user-confirmation gate, and the rebase.
117	
118	If the working tree is already clean, skip this step.
119	
120	### Step 4: Squash to a coherent set of commits
121	
122	**Hard gate: squash before roborev, roborev before the user-confirmation gate, confirmation before push.** All three must happen before the branch hits `origin` so the review (and the merge) operate on the final history, not a noisy timeline.
123	
124	```bash
125	git log main..HEAD --oneline
126	```
127	
128	- **Default to one commit per PR.** Multi-commit PRs are only OK when each commit is independently reviewable and the slices land in order.
129	- Squash with `git rebase -i main` or `git reset --soft main && git commit`. Never use `--no-edit` flags that bypass message review.
130	- The squashed commit message mirrors the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) and captures the motivation in the body. No Conventional Commits prefix.
131	- If the branch already has a single commit (or each existing commit is independently reviewable and ordered), skip the rebase but still confirm the count before moving on.
132	- **Never force-push to a shared branch to squash after publication.** Squash *before* the first push.
133	
134	### Step 5: Run relevant tests locally, then roborev review before drafting
135	
136	**Roborev reviews the diff; it does not execute the test suite.** A clean roborev pass says nothing about whether the code runs — it has caught logic/quality issues while a hardcoded assertion in a test file was still broken. Before roborev, run whatever tests cover the changed files:
137	
138	- Identify affected tests by mirroring the changed path under `tests/` (many repos mirror source layout — a change to `pkg/foo.py` often has a matching `tests/.../test_foo.py`) and/or `grep -rn` the changed file's distinctive strings (a literal like an `if:` condition, a flag name) across `tests/` to catch assertions on exact values.
139	- Run the narrowest test target that covers the change (in a uv-based Python repo, `uv run pytest tests/<mirrored-path>`; otherwise the repo's own test command) — full-suite runs are fine too, but don't skip this step because CI will "catch it anyway": local runs take seconds, CI takes minutes.
140	- If a test fails, fix it now and fold the fix into the same commit (Step 3/4), *before* running roborev — don't push and let CI discover it.
141	
142	**Hard gate: do not draft the PR or move toward `git push` until roborev has run and either reported clean or been explicitly acknowledged by the user.** This applies even if the change feels trivial, even if the diff is one line, and even if the user has not asked for review explicitly — the skill always runs roborev before the user is asked to approve a draft.
143	
144	With the squashed commit in place but the branch still local, run a local AI code review with roborev so findings surface *before* the user sees a draft and *before* GitHub sees the diff. Invoke the `roborev` executable directly with the `--wait` flag; Git aliases are optional conveniences and may not exist in cloud sandboxes:
145	
146	```bash
147	roborev review --wait
148	```
149	
150	- `--wait` is **required**, not optional — it blocks until the review completes so findings are available before the draft is shown. Do not run `roborev review` without `--wait`.
151	- A bare `roborev review` — or a leftover post-commit auto-review hook — only **enqueues a background daemon job and returns before a verdict exists**. An enqueue is not a pass: if HEAD already has a queued or running background review, block on it (`roborev review --wait`, or `roborev wait` for the already-enqueued job) so an actual verdict is in hand before drafting. Never report "review enqueued" or a missing verdict as clean.
152	- Capture the outcome (clean, N findings fixed in M rounds, N findings unresolved, unavailable) — Step 8 surfaces it inside the draft preview so the user can see the gate was walked.
153	- **Review loop (no permission prompts):** if roborev surfaces findings, fix them yourself without asking — **every severity counts**, including low and nit. Do not stop, summarize, or ask "fix these?" / "defer or proceed?" because findings are low severity. Fix as many as possible that are small in scope: a wording or error-message change, a missing test case, a missing guard, a rename, a local refactor inside the changed function. Do not fix findings that would reshape the surrounding design, change public interfaces, or touch files outside this PR's scope; for those only, report them to the user with the reason they were not fixed. Put the fixes in a follow-up commit, re-squash (Step 4), and re-run `roborev review --wait` (this step). Repeat until a run comes back clean or only out-of-scope findings remain. Do not ask "fix and rerun?" — that is the default action.
154	- **Loop cap:** stop after 3 fix rounds. If findings remain, or a finding would need a product or design decision rather than a code fix, stop looping and list the unresolved findings in the Step 8 draft preview, so the user decides at the single approval gate. Never amend or force-push past findings silently.
155	- If roborev is unavailable (command not installed, no network), say so explicitly to the user and ask whether to proceed without review. Do not silently skip.
156	- For deeper fix/refine loops, consult the repo's roborev guide skill if it ships one.
157	
158	### Step 6: Draft the title
159	
160	The title is a formal, sentence-cased statement of **why this change exists** — not a conventional commit subject. A reviewer scanning the PR list should understand the *motivation*, not just the area of code touched.
161	
162	Rules:
163	
164	- **Formal, sentence case.** "Eliminate duplicated Attio retry logic across five call sites" — not "attio retry refactor".
165	- **Lead with the why, not the what.** Prefer the problem solved or the outcome enabled over the mechanical change. "Unblock Linear → Attio sync from rate-limit drift" beats "Add retry decorator to Attio client".
166	- **No Conventional Commits prefix.** Do **not** use `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, etc. Even if recent commits or PRs use them, PR titles in this ecosystem are full sentences. Commit messages and PR titles are different surfaces.
167	- **Under 70 characters where possible**, but clarity wins over brevity — GitHub truncates in list views, so front-load the most important words.
168	- **Specific.** "Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts" — not "Bug fix" or "Improvements".
169	- **No ticket IDs in the title.** They go in Links.
170	- **No trailing period.**
171	- **Avoid bare imperative verbs** like "Add", "Fix", "Update" as the first word when a why-framing is possible. They're allowed when the why genuinely is the action (e.g., a clear bugfix), but check first whether the motivation can lead instead.
172	
173	Good vs. bad title shapes:
174	
175	| Bad (conventional / what-focused) | Good (formal / why-focused) |
176	| --- | --- |
177	| `feat: add retry decorator` | `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear sync` |
178	| `fix: pagination bug` | `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts` |
179	| `refactor: clean up attio client` | `Eliminate divergent retry behavior across Attio call sites` |
180	| `chore: bump deps` | `Bump httpx to 0.27 to pick up the connection-pool leak fix` |
181	
182	### Step 7: Draft the description
183	
184	Use this template. **Drop sections that have nothing meaningful in them** — a section containing "None" or "N/A" is worse than no section.
185	
186	```markdown
187	## Why
188	<1-3 paragraphs. Lead with the problem or constraint. State the motivation. Reference upstream context (ticket, spec) by link, not paraphrase. The reviewer should finish this section understanding what would happen if the PR were *not* merged.>
189	
190	## Trade-offs
191	<Only if there were meaningful alternatives. Format: "Chose X over Y because Z." Skip if the approach was obvious or there was only one reasonable way.>
192	
193	## Risks
194	<What could break that isn't already covered by tests. Note rollback path if non-trivial. Skip for clearly low-risk changes (docs, comments, isolated refactors with full coverage).>
195	
196	## Test plan
197	<Reasoning, not output. "Exercised X path with Y inputs because Z is the highest-risk surface." If full unit coverage exists and the change is small/obvious, skip this section.>
198	
199	## Links
200	- Linear: [TEAM-NNN](https://linear.app/...)
201	- Spec: design/backlog-...-spec-01.md
202	- Plan: design/backlog-...-plan-01.md
203	- Related PRs: #NNN
204	- Closes #NNN (only when Step 2 confirmed this PR fully resolves a same-repo GitHub issue)
205	```
206	
207	Section guidance:
208	
209	| Section | Required? | When to drop it |
210	| --- | --- | --- |
211	| Why | Always | Never. If you can't write a specific one, the work isn't ready. |
212	| Trade-offs | When meaningful alternatives existed | Obvious one-way changes, fixes to clear bugs |
213	| Risks | When the change has non-trivial blast radius | Docs, comments, isolated refactors with coverage |
214	| Test plan | When testing required judgment calls | Small changes with full unit coverage |
215	| Links | If any upstream artifact exists | True greenfield work with no ticket, spec, or predecessor PR |
216	
217	### Step 8: Show the draft. Wait for confirmation. (Single approval gate before push.)
218	
219	**This is the only user-approval gate in the workflow, and it sits immediately before `git push`.** Steps 3–5 (commit, squash, roborev) must already be complete by the time you reach it — by construction the agent cannot honor a "yes" without having walked the roborev gate first.
220	
221	Show the draft title, the draft body, **and the roborev outcome** so the user can see the gate was walked. Even if the user said "create a PR", they agreed to the action, not blind-trusted your draft.
222	
223	**Shortcut:** If the user re-sends this *exact* create_pr prompt verbatim, or an explicit approval phrase like "create/open the PR now," immediately after the agent has already shown a draft under this step, treat that as the Step 8 approval — proceed exactly as a "yes" would (Steps 9–13), don't re-run Steps 1–7 to produce a fresh draft. Anything else — a revision request, a question about the draft, or a paraphrase — is not the shortcut; treat it as normal feedback and re-show the draft.
224	
225	Format the preview as:
226	
227	```text
228	Title: <draft title>
229	
230	Body:
231	---
232	<draft body>
233	---
234	
235	Roborev: <clean (after M fix rounds) | N findings unresolved (list them) | unavailable (reason)>
236	
237	Push and create this PR? (or edit before I submit)
238	```
239	
240	The roborev line is mandatory — never omit it. If it shows "unavailable", the user is implicitly being asked to proceed without review.
241	
242	If the user requests edits, revise and re-show. Don't auto-submit. A "yes" here authorizes closing or linking the GitHub issue (Step 9), the rebase (Step 10), the push (Step 11), and the PR creation (Step 12) — proceed through all of them without re-prompting (pausing only if the rebase hits conflicts).
243	
244	### Step 9: Note the GitHub issue disposition
245	
246	If Step 2 identified a GitHub issue this PR addresses, carry its disposition forward — the actual action happens in Step 12b, once a PR URL exists:
247	
248	- **Same-repo issue, fully resolved by this PR** — the `Closes #NNN` line already lives in the PR body (Step 7's Links section). Nothing further is needed here: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges into `main`. Don't `gh issue close` it now — the fix isn't on `main` yet.
249	- **Cross-repo issue, or only partially resolved** — GitHub's closing keywords don't work across repos and shouldn't be used for partial work. Remember to leave a linking comment in Step 12b instead of closing it.
250	- **Ambiguous whether this PR fully resolves it** — this should already have been resolved in Step 2; if it wasn't, ask the user now rather than guessing at merge-closing behavior.
251	- Skip silently if no GitHub issue was identified in Step 2.
252	- Already authorized by the Step 8 "yes" — don't re-prompt.
253	
254	### Step 10: Rebase onto the latest base (last step before opening the PR)
255	
256	**This is the final step before the PR is opened.** Immediately before pushing, rebase the branch onto the freshest base so the PR opens against current `main` and merge conflicts surface here — locally, where they're cheap to resolve — instead of in GitHub's merge UI.
257	
258	This must happen **before** the first push (Step 11), not after. Rebasing a branch that's already on `origin` would require a force-push, which is forbidden without explicit user approval.
259	
260	```bash
261	git fetch origin
262	git rebase origin/main   # or the confirmed base branch from pre-flight
263	```
264	
265	- If the rebase is clean, proceed to Step 11.
266	- If the rebase hits conflicts, **stop and surface them to the user.** Resolve them (or have the user resolve them), then re-run Steps 4–5 (re-squash if needed, re-run `roborev review --wait`) so the review reflects the rebased history. Never `git rebase --skip` or abandon conflicting hunks silently.
267	- If the branch is already up to date with the base, the rebase is a no-op — proceed.
268	
269	### Step 11: Push the branch
270	
271	Once the rebase is clean, push the branch to `origin` with upstream tracking.
272	
273	```bash
274	git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
275	```
276	
277	Confirm the push succeeded before moving on. If it fails (auth, protected branch, non-fast-forward), surface the error and stop — do not force-push.
278	
279	### Step 12: Create the PR
280	
281	**Hard gate before running `gh pr create`: for every same-repo GitHub issue Step 2 determined this PR fully resolves, mechanically verify the drafted body contains a `Closes #NNN` / `Fixes #NNN` / `Resolves #NNN` line for *that specific* issue number before shelling out — one PR can fully resolve more than one issue, and each needs its own closing reference, not just the first.** This is a real known failure mode, not a hypothetical: gtm-sdk#609 was fully fixed by gtm-sdk#628, but the drafted body only listed "gtm-sdk#609" under Links without a closing keyword, so GitHub never auto-closed it and it sat open until manually closed later. A "the plan said to add it" belief is not sufficient — grep the actual string you're about to pass to `--body` for the pattern before running the command, once per fully-resolved issue number:
282	
283	```bash
284	grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY"
285	```
286	
287	`\b` is not portable to the BSD `grep` on macOS — use the `([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` form above instead, which matches the same "word boundary or end of string" intent on both BSD and GNU grep.
288	
289	If that grep fails for any fully-resolved issue number, **stop and fix the body** — don't proceed to `gh pr create` with a body that silently downgraded to a bare reference. If Step 2 flagged partial/cross-repo instead, the grep is expected to fail and that's correct — don't add the keyword in that case.
290	
291	To make this checkable, assign the HEREDOC to `PR_BODY` first, grep that exact variable, then pass it to `--body` — don't construct the body inline in the `gh pr create` call, since there's nothing to grep before shelling out:
292	
293	```bash
294	PR_BODY="$(cat <<'EOF'
295	## Why
296	... (real newlines, not \n)
297	EOF
298	)"
299	
300	for ISSUE_NUMBER in "${FULLY_RESOLVED_ISSUE_NUMBERS[@]}"; do  # every issue Step 2 flagged as fully resolved
301	  grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY" || {
302	    echo "missing closing keyword for #${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >&2
303	    exit 1
304	  }
305	done
306	
307	gh pr create --title "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup that double-charged credits" --body "$PR_BODY"
308	```
309	
310	Return the PR URL to the user. Don't add follow-up commentary unless the user asks — the URL is the work product.
311	
312	### Step 12b: Link the GitHub issue, if Step 9 deferred it
313	
314	Only applies when Step 9 flagged a **cross-repo or partially-resolved** issue — the fully-resolved same-repo case already carries its `Closes #NNN` in the PR body and needs no action here.
315	
316	```bash
317	gh issue comment <number> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>"                    # same-repo, partial
318	gh issue comment <number> --repo <owner/repo> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>" # cross-repo — use the owner/repo saved in Step 2
319	```
320	
321	- `<PR URL>` is the output from Step 12 — this step cannot run before Step 12 for exactly that reason.
322	- Do not close the issue yourself; partial or cross-repo work isn't the maintainer's signal to close it.
323	- Skip silently if Step 9 found nothing to do here.
324	
325	### Step 13: Suggest the merge once tests and checks pass
326	
327	Merging is never automatic. Once the PR is open, check its status with a single call (`gh pr checks <pr-number>`). When tests and required checks have passed, suggest merging with the GitHub CLI and wait for the user to say yes:
328	
329	```bash
330	gh pr merge <pr-number> --squash
331	```
332	
333	- Do not poll in a loop. If checks are still running, report that and stop; the user can ask again later.
334	- Do not log in to, configure, or call any merge-queue service. If `gh` is not authenticated, say so and stop.
335	- Never pass `--admin` or `--auto` unless the user asks for it.
336	
337	## Modifiers: drafts, reviewers, labels
338	
339	`gh pr create` accepts modifiers that don't affect the description but matter for the PR's lifecycle. Don't auto-set any of these; only pass what the user explicitly asks for:
340	
341	| Flag | When |
342	| --- | --- |
343	| `--draft` | User says "draft", or commit history shows clear in-progress markers ("WIP", "spike"). |
344	| `--reviewer <handle>` | Only when the user names reviewers. Don't guess. |
345	| `--label <name>` | Only labels that exist (`gh label list`). Invented labels silently no-op. |
346	| `--assignee <handle>` | Default to `@me` unless told otherwise. |
347	| `--base <branch>` | Only override the default branch when the user says so. |
348	
349	## Anti-patterns
350	
351	These show up in autogenerated PR descriptions and this skill must actively avoid them. Several come from defaults baked into other tools — including the default `gh pr create` template suggested by the Bash tool — and this skill overrides them.
352	
353	### Don't summarize the diff
354	
355	```markdown
356	## Summary
357	- Added `retry_with_backoff` helper in `apollo/client.py`
358	- Updated `enrich_account` to use it
359	- Added 3 unit tests in `test_apollo.py`
360	```
361	
362	The reviewer is about to read the diff. This is duplicate work that rots the moment the diff changes. Replace with **Why**.
363	
364	### Don't write empty sections
365	
366	```markdown
367	## Risks
368	None.
369	
370	## Test plan
371	Tested locally.
372	```
373	
374	"None" and "Tested locally" carry zero signal. Drop the section.
375	
376	### Don't add AI attribution
377	
378	The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) prohibit AI attribution in commits and PRs.
379	**Never** emit:
380	
381	- `Co-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>`
382	- `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](...)`
383	- Any "Generated by ..." or "Powered by ..." footer
384	
385	The Bash tool's default PR template includes the 🤖 footer. **Strip it.** This skill overrides that default.
386	
387	### Don't restate the title
388	
389	If the title is "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup", the description shouldn't open with "This PR fixes a race in the Apollo enrichment dedup logic." Start the Why with the problem, not a rephrase.
390	
391	### Don't pad with boilerplate
392	
393	- "This PR makes some improvements to ..."
394	- "As discussed offline, ..."
395	- "Cleaning up some technical debt ..."
396	
397	If you can't write a specific Why, pause and ask the user. Vague motivation is a tell that the work isn't ready for review.
398	
399	### Don't paste test output
400	
401	The Test plan section is about the *reasoning* behind what was tested. A reviewer can run the tests. They cannot rederive your reasoning from the output.
402	
403	### Don't include "Closes #NNN" without confirming
404	
405	GitHub auto-closes referenced issues on merge. Only use `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves` keywords if Step 2 confirmed the PR fully resolves a **same-repo** issue. For partial work or a cross-repo issue, mention it in Links instead and leave a linking comment on the issue in Step 12b — no magic keyword. Skipping the confirmation in Step 2 is a bug, not a safe default: it leaves the issue open with no trace back to the PR that addressed it.
406	
407	### Don't autopilot the PR submission
408	
409	Even if the user said "create a PR for this", they agreed to the action, not to a specific draft. Show the draft, wait for confirmation, then submit.
410	
411	## Examples
412	
413	### Example 1: Small bug fix — Why + Links only
414	
415	**Title:** `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts`
416	
417	**Body:**
418	
419	```markdown
420	## Why
421	The Apollo `search_people` paginator was dropping the last page of results because the cursor check used `>` instead of `>=`. Affected every batch where total results were an exact multiple of page_size — roughly 10% of runs. Caught when a TAM build was missing ~50 known contacts ([AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)).
422	
423	## Links
424	- Linear: [AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)
425	```
426	
427	(Trade-offs, Risks, Test plan dropped — small obvious fix, full coverage exists.)
428	
429	### Example 2: Refactor — Why + Trade-offs + Risks + Links
430	
431	**Title:** `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear → Attio sync`
432	
433	**Body:**
434	
435	```markdown
436	## Why
437	Five call sites in `libs/attio/` were duplicating retry/backoff logic, and each had drifted: `update_person` retried on 5xx but not 429; `create_person` retried on 429 but with no backoff; `list_workspaces` did no retry at all. The new Linear → Attio sync was about to become the sixth divergent copy.
438	
439	Pulling the logic into `@retry_with_backoff` lets callers opt in with one line and ensures consistent behavior across all Attio writes.
440	
441	## Trade-offs
442	Considered `tenacity` instead. Rejected because the call sites already have idiosyncratic logic — custom backoff that respects Attio's `Retry-After` header — that `tenacity` would require a custom wait strategy to express. The hand-rolled decorator is ~30 lines and stays close to the Attio-specific behavior.
443	
444	## Risks
445	Changes the *shape* of exceptions that bubble up: `AttioRateLimit` is now wrapped in `RetryExhausted` after N attempts. Two existing callers caught `AttioRateLimit` directly; both updated in this PR. Grep for `AttioRateLimit` returns no other matches.
446	
447	## Links
448	- Linear: [AI-2891](https://linear.app/...)
449	- Spec: design/backlog-202604010000-attio_retry_decorator-spec-01.md
450	```
451	
452	### Example 3: Bad → Good
453	
454	**Bad:**
455	
456	```markdown
457	## Summary
458	- Added retry decorator
459	- Updated 5 Attio call sites
460	- Removed duplicate retry code
461	- Added tests
462	
463	## Test plan
464	- [x] Ran tests
465	- [x] Tested locally
466	
467	🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
468	```
469	
470	What's wrong: the Summary paraphrases the diff, the Test plan has no reasoning, the AI footer is forbidden, and there's no motivation a reviewer can use to evaluate the change.
471	
472	**Good:** see Example 2.

474	## Failure modes and recovery
475	
476	| What happened | What to do |
477	| --- | --- |
478	| Linear MCP unavailable or ticket not found | Continue without the Linear context. Note in Links: "Linear ticket: AI-NNN (MCP unavailable at draft time)" and let the user fill in. |
479	| Branch doesn't match a Linear pattern | Skip the Linear lookup. Rely on design artifacts and conversation. |
480	| No design artifact, no ticket, no clear Why from the conversation | Stop. Ask the user: "I can't establish a specific Why for this PR from the available context. Can you summarize the motivation in 1-2 sentences?" |
481	| `gh pr create` fails (auth, network, no remote) | Surface the error to the user. Don't retry without diagnosing. |
482	| User rejects the draft | Take their feedback and rewrite. Don't argue. |
483	| User wants to skip the confirmation step | Honor it — but require an explicit "skip confirmation" or "just create it" from them. Default is to confirm. |
484	
485	## Common pitfalls
486	
487	| Pitfall | Why it bites | Fix |
488	| --- | --- | --- |
489	| Drafting before pre-flight checks | PR opened against stale base, with uncommitted work left behind | Run the pre-flight batch first |
490	| Not checking for an existing PR | Duplicate PR, or `gh pr create` errors out | Always `gh pr view` first |
491	| Pasting the Linear ticket verbatim | Description becomes a wall of duplicated text | Paraphrase the problem statement; link the rest |
492	| Filling all sections regardless of signal | Skim-defeating filler | Drop sections that don't carry meaning |
493	| Autopiloting `gh pr create` | Premature publication; harder to retract than to delay | Show draft, wait for confirmation |
494	| Inheriting the default 🤖 footer | Violates the repo's no-AI-attribution rule | Strip it from the body |
495	| Trusting a clean roborev as proof the code runs | Roborev reviews the diff, not test execution — a hardcoded test assertion (e.g. a literal YAML `if:` string) can still fail in CI | Run the mirrored test file / grep for affected literals before roborev (Step 5) |
496	| Using "WIP" in title instead of `--draft` | Title noise; doesn't actually mark the PR as draft | Use `gh pr create --draft` and a clean title |
497	| Linking to the PR's own branch name as "context" | The branch is implicit; this is noise | Only link to artifacts that aren't already obvious from the PR |
498	| Forgetting the linked GitHub issue entirely | Issue lingers open after merge with no trace back to the PR that fixed it | Resolve it in Step 2, `Closes #NNN` in Step 7, record disposition in Step 9, comment in Step 12b |
499	| Drafting `Closes #NNN` in Step 7 but the final body sent to `gh pr create` drops it (edits, re-drafts, template drift) | Issue never auto-closes even though Step 2/9 correctly flagged full resolution — happened for real on gtm-sdk#609/#628 | Step 12's mechanical grep gate on the literal `--body` string, not on what Step 7 intended to write |
500	
501	## Red flags (stop and rethink)
502	
503	- **About to `git push` without running `roborev review --wait` first.** This is the repository-wide roborev gate defined in the repo's agent instructions; no PR should skip it.
504	- **About to `git push` with more commits than the PR needs.** Squash to a coherent set first (Step 4); don't rely on GitHub's "Squash and merge" button to clean up history before review.
505	- Drafting a PR with no Linear ticket, no design artifact, and no conversation-derived motivation.
506	- Writing more than 3 paragraphs in Why. If you need that much, the work is probably two PRs.
507	- Including a `## Summary` section. This is the default template's tell — replace with `## Why`.
508	- Including a 🤖 footer.
509	- More than 5 bullets in any one section. Each bullet should be load-bearing.
510	- A title that ends in a period, or starts with "Update", "Fix some", "Misc", "Various".
511	- A title that uses a Conventional Commits prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). PR titles are formal sentences, not commit subjects.
512	- A title that describes *what* the diff does (e.g., "Add X helper", "Refactor Y module") when a *why* framing was available.

526	# Creating Pull Requests
527	
528	## The principle: why over what
529	
530	A PR description's job is to give the reviewer what the diff *can't*: motivation, alternatives considered, risks worth scrutinizing, and a trail back to the originating context. The diff itself is the source of truth for what changed — paraphrasing it in the description is duplicate work that rots the moment someone force-pushes.
531	
532	Concretely:
533	
534	- Lead with the **problem**, not the change.
535	- Name the **alternatives** you considered, briefly. Skip if there were no meaningful ones.
536	- Call out what reviewers should **scrutinize**, not what they should take on faith.
537	- Link the **breadcrumb trail** — Linear ticket, design spec/plan, predecessor PR.
538	- **Never** summarize the diff. The reviewer is about to read it.
539	
540	A reader who skims your description should walk away with the mental model needed to read the diff with intention.
541	
542	## Workflow
543	
544	### Step 1: Pre-flight checks
545	
546	Before drafting, run these in a single batch of parallel `Bash` calls:
547	
548	```bash
549	git status                                          # working tree clean?
550	git branch --show-current                           # current branch?
551	git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null  # is there a remote tracking ref?
552	git log @{upstream}..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null     # any unpushed commits?
553	git log main..HEAD --oneline                        # commits beyond main?
554	git diff main...HEAD --stat                         # surface area?
555	gh pr view --json url,state 2>/dev/null             # does a PR already exist?
556	gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name  # confirm base
557	```
558	
559	Stop and surface the problem to the user if any of these is true:
560	
561	- The working tree has uncommitted changes — ask the user whether to commit, stash, or abandon.
562	- The branch has no upstream / is not pushed — confirm with the user before pushing.
563	- The branch has zero commits beyond the base — there's nothing to PR.
564	- A PR already exists for this branch — use `gh pr edit` to update it, not `gh pr create`.
565	
566	Don't paper over these by force-pushing, amending, or running `git push -f`. The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) apply: destructive operations need explicit user approval.
567	
568	### Step 2: Gather context for the "Why"
569	
570	A strong Why section comes from upstream artifacts, not from the diff. Pull from these sources in parallel where possible:
571	
572	**Linear ticket** — if the branch name matches `(feature|agent)/<team>-<number>-<slug>` (e.g., `feature/ai-268-foo`, `agent/eng-1234-bar`):
573	
574	1. Extract the ticket ID with a regex like `[A-Z]+-\d+` (case-insensitive).
575	2. Read it via `mcp__linear__get_issue` with the identifier.
576	3. Lift the problem statement and acceptance criteria into the Why section — **paraphrase, don't paste**. A wall of quoted ticket text isn't a PR description.
577	4. Save the URL for the Links section.
578	
579	Skip the Linear lookup when the repo doesn't use Linear (no Linear MCP configured, no matching branch pattern) — rely on the sources below.
580	
581	**GitHub issue** — if the user linked or named a GitHub issue this session (a URL, `#NNN`, or an issue the branch was created for, e.g., `conductor/gtm-sdk-issue-608`):
582	
583	1. Note whether it's same-repo or cross-repo (a bare `#NNN` or number is same-repo; a URL or `owner/repo#NNN` names the repo explicitly — keep that `owner/repo` around for every later step). Fetch it with `gh issue view <number>` for a same-repo issue, or `gh issue view <number> --repo <owner/repo>` otherwise, to confirm it's still open and pull the problem statement into the Why section — paraphrase, don't paste.
584	2. Ask yourself (and, if unclear, the user) whether this PR **fully** resolves the issue or only partial work. Carry that determination into Step 7's Links section and Step 9.
585	3. Save the issue reference for the Links section either way.
586	
587	**Design artifacts** — scan `design/` (when the repo uses the design-artifact convention) for backlog/done files matching the branch topic:
588	
589	```bash
590	ls "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/design/" 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "<topic-keyword>"
591	```
592	
593	- `*-spec-*.md` files carry motivation, constraints, trade-offs.
594	- `*-plan-*.md` files carry scope (and by elision, what's out of scope).
595	- Read the matching artifact in full before drafting.
596	
597	**Git history**:
598	
599	- `git log main..HEAD --format='%s%n%b%n---'` — commit subjects and bodies often capture in-flight decisions better than the final diff.
600	
601	**Current conversation**:
602	
603	- If the user discussed alternatives, made decisions mid-flight, or set constraints earlier in this session, those belong in Trade-offs or Risks.
604	
605	If none of these sources establishes a clear Why, **stop and ask the user**. Don't fabricate motivation — a confident-sounding-but-vague Why is worse than asking.
606	
607	### Step 3: Commit local changes
608	
609	If the pre-flight check surfaced uncommitted changes that belong in this PR, commit them **before** running roborev — roborev reviews committed history, not the working tree, so uncommitted edits would be invisible to it.
610	
611	- Stage only the files that belong in this PR. Skip tool-local cruft (e.g., `.agents/`, `.claude/`, Conductor-local files) unless the user explicitly opts in.
612	- Commit without asking for approval: run `git commit` directly once the files are staged. The commit message should mirror the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) — not a Conventional Commits subject. The Step 8 draft approval is still the only user-approval gate before push.
613	- Do **not** push yet. Push happens in Step 11, after squash, roborev, the user-confirmation gate, and the rebase.
614	
615	If the working tree is already clean, skip this step.
616	
617	### Step 4: Squash to a coherent set of commits
618	
619	**Hard gate: squash before roborev, roborev before the user-confirmation gate, confirmation before push.** All three must happen before the branch hits `origin` so the review (and the merge) operate on the final history, not a noisy timeline.
620	
621	```bash
622	git log main..HEAD --oneline
623	```
624	
625	- **Default to one commit per PR.** Multi-commit PRs are only OK when each commit is independently reviewable and the slices land in order.
626	- Squash with `git rebase -i main` or `git reset --soft main && git commit`. Never use `--no-edit` flags that bypass message review.
627	- The squashed commit message mirrors the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) and captures the motivation in the body. No Conventional Commits prefix.
628	- If the branch already has a single commit (or each existing commit is independently reviewable and ordered), skip the rebase but still confirm the count before moving on.
629	- **Never force-push to a shared branch to squash after publication.** Squash *before* the first push.
630	
631	### Step 5: Run relevant tests locally, then roborev review before drafting
632	
633	**Roborev reviews the diff; it does not execute the test suite.** A clean roborev pass says nothing about whether the code runs — it has caught logic/quality issues while a hardcoded assertion in a test file was still broken. Before roborev, run whatever tests cover the changed files:
634	
635	- Identify affected tests by mirroring the changed path under `tests/` (many repos mirror source layout — a change to `pkg/foo.py` often has a matching `tests/.../test_foo.py`) and/or `grep -rn` the changed file's distinctive strings (a literal like an `if:` condition, a flag name) across `tests/` to catch assertions on exact values.
636	- Run the narrowest test target that covers the change (in a uv-based Python repo, `uv run pytest tests/<mirrored-path>`; otherwise the repo's own test command) — full-suite runs are fine too, but don't skip this step because CI will "catch it anyway": local runs take seconds, CI takes minutes.
637	- If a test fails, fix it now and fold the fix into the same commit (Step 3/4), *before* running roborev — don't push and let CI discover it.
638	
639	**Hard gate: do not draft the PR or move toward `git push` until roborev has run and either reported clean or been explicitly acknowledged by the user.** This applies even if the change feels trivial, even if the diff is one line, and even if the user has not asked for review explicitly — the skill always runs roborev before the user is asked to approve a draft.
640	
641	With the squashed commit in place but the branch still local, run a local AI code review with roborev so findings surface *before* the user sees a draft and *before* GitHub sees the diff. Invoke the `roborev` executable directly with the `--wait` flag; Git aliases are optional conveniences and may not exist in cloud sandboxes:
642	
643	```bash
644	roborev review --wait
645	```
646	
647	- `--wait` is **required**, not optional — it blocks until the review completes so findings are available before the draft is shown. Do not run `roborev review` without `--wait`.
648	- A bare `roborev review` — or a leftover post-commit auto-review hook — only **enqueues a background daemon job and returns before a verdict exists**. An enqueue is not a pass: if HEAD already has a queued or running background review, block on it (`roborev review --wait`, or `roborev wait` for the already-enqueued job) so an actual verdict is in hand before drafting. Never report "review enqueued" or a missing verdict as clean.
649	- Capture the outcome (clean, N findings fixed in M rounds, N findings unresolved, unavailable) — Step 8 surfaces it inside the draft preview so the user can see the gate was walked.
650	- **Review loop (no permission prompts):** if roborev surfaces findings, fix them yourself without asking — **every severity counts**, including low and nit. Do not stop, summarize, or ask "fix these?" / "defer or proceed?" because findings are low severity. Fix as many as possible that are small in scope: a wording or error-message change, a missing test case, a missing guard, a rename, a local refactor inside the changed function. Do not fix findings that would reshape the surrounding design, change public interfaces, or touch files outside this PR's scope; for those only, report them to the user with the reason they were not fixed. Put the fixes in a follow-up commit, re-squash (Step 4), and re-run `roborev review --wait` (this step). Repeat until a run comes back clean or only out-of-scope findings remain. Do not ask "fix and rerun?" — that is the default action.
651	- **Loop cap:** stop after 3 fix rounds. If findings remain, or a finding would need a product or design decision rather than a code fix, stop looping and list the unresolved findings in the Step 8 draft preview, so the user decides at the single approval gate. Never amend or force-push past findings silently.
652	- If roborev is unavailable (command not installed, no network), say so explicitly to the user and ask whether to proceed without review. Do not silently skip.
653	- For deeper fix/refine loops, consult the repo's roborev guide skill if it ships one.
654	
655	### Step 6: Draft the title
656	
657	The title is a formal, sentence-cased statement of **why this change exists** — not a conventional commit subject. A reviewer scanning the PR list should understand the *motivation*, not just the area of code touched.
658	
659	Rules:
660	
661	- **Formal, sentence case.** "Eliminate duplicated Attio retry logic across five call sites" — not "attio retry refactor".
662	- **Lead with the why, not the what.** Prefer the problem solved or the outcome enabled over the mechanical change. "Unblock Linear → Attio sync from rate-limit drift" beats "Add retry decorator to Attio client".
663	- **No Conventional Commits prefix.** Do **not** use `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, etc. Even if recent commits or PRs use them, PR titles in this ecosystem are full sentences. Commit messages and PR titles are different surfaces.
664	- **Under 70 characters where possible**, but clarity wins over brevity — GitHub truncates in list views, so front-load the most important words.
665	- **Specific.** "Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts" — not "Bug fix" or "Improvements".
666	- **No ticket IDs in the title.** They go in Links.
667	- **No trailing period.**
668	- **Avoid bare imperative verbs** like "Add", "Fix", "Update" as the first word when a why-framing is possible. They're allowed when the why genuinely is the action (e.g., a clear bugfix), but check first whether the motivation can lead instead.
669	
670	Good vs. bad title shapes:
671	
672	| Bad (conventional / what-focused) | Good (formal / why-focused) |
673	| --- | --- |
674	| `feat: add retry decorator` | `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear sync` |
675	| `fix: pagination bug` | `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts` |
676	| `refactor: clean up attio client` | `Eliminate divergent retry behavior across Attio call sites` |
677	| `chore: bump deps` | `Bump httpx to 0.27 to pick up the connection-pool leak fix` |
678	
679	### Step 7: Draft the description
680	
681	Use this template. **Drop sections that have nothing meaningful in them** — a section containing "None" or "N/A" is worse than no section.
682	
683	```markdown
684	## Why
685	<1-3 paragraphs. Lead with the problem or constraint. State the motivation. Reference upstream context (ticket, spec) by link, not paraphrase. The reviewer should finish this section understanding what would happen if the PR were *not* merged.>
686	
687	## Trade-offs
688	<Only if there were meaningful alternatives. Format: "Chose X over Y because Z." Skip if the approach was obvious or there was only one reasonable way.>
689	
690	## Risks
691	<What could break that isn't already covered by tests. Note rollback path if non-trivial. Skip for clearly low-risk changes (docs, comments, isolated refactors with full coverage).>
692	
693	## Test plan
694	<Reasoning, not output. "Exercised X path with Y inputs because Z is the highest-risk surface." If full unit coverage exists and the change is small/obvious, skip this section.>
695	
696	## Links
697	- Linear: [TEAM-NNN](https://linear.app/...)
698	- Spec: design/backlog-...-spec-01.md
699	- Plan: design/backlog-...-plan-01.md
700	- Related PRs: #NNN
701	- Closes #NNN (only when Step 2 confirmed this PR fully resolves a same-repo GitHub issue)
702	```
703	
704	Section guidance:
705	
706	| Section | Required? | When to drop it |
707	| --- | --- | --- |
708	| Why | Always | Never. If you can't write a specific one, the work isn't ready. |
709	| Trade-offs | When meaningful alternatives existed | Obvious one-way changes, fixes to clear bugs |
710	| Risks | When the change has non-trivial blast radius | Docs, comments, isolated refactors with coverage |
711	| Test plan | When testing required judgment calls | Small changes with full unit coverage |
712	| Links | If any upstream artifact exists | True greenfield work with no ticket, spec, or predecessor PR |
713	
714	### Step 8: Show the draft. Wait for confirmation. (Single approval gate before push.)
715	
716	**This is the only user-approval gate in the workflow, and it sits immediately before `git push`.** Steps 3–5 (commit, squash, roborev) must already be complete by the time you reach it — by construction the agent cannot honor a "yes" without having walked the roborev gate first.
717	
718	Show the draft title, the draft body, **and the roborev outcome** so the user can see the gate was walked. Even if the user said "create a PR", they agreed to the action, not blind-trusted your draft.
719	
720	**Shortcut:** If the user re-sends this *exact* create_pr prompt verbatim, or an explicit approval phrase like "create/open the PR now," immediately after the agent has already shown a draft under this step, treat that as the Step 8 approval — proceed exactly as a "yes" would (Steps 9–13), don't re-run Steps 1–7 to produce a fresh draft. Anything else — a revision request, a question about the draft, or a paraphrase — is not the shortcut; treat it as normal feedback and re-show the draft.
721	
722	Format the preview as:
723	
724	```text
725	Title: <draft title>
726	
727	Body:
728	---
729	<draft body>
730	---
731	
732	Roborev: <clean (after M fix rounds) | N findings unresolved (list them) | unavailable (reason)>
733	
734	Push and create this PR? (or edit before I submit)
735	```
736	
737	The roborev line is mandatory — never omit it. If it shows "unavailable", the user is implicitly being asked to proceed without review.
738	
739	If the user requests edits, revise and re-show. Don't auto-submit. A "yes" here authorizes closing or linking the GitHub issue (Step 9), the rebase (Step 10), the push (Step 11), and the PR creation (Step 12) — proceed through all of them without re-prompting (pausing only if the rebase hits conflicts).
740	
741	### Step 9: Note the GitHub issue disposition
742	
743	If Step 2 identified a GitHub issue this PR addresses, carry its disposition forward — the actual action happens in Step 12b, once a PR URL exists:
744	
745	- **Same-repo issue, fully resolved by this PR** — the `Closes #NNN` line already lives in the PR body (Step 7's Links section). Nothing further is needed here: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges into `main`. Don't `gh issue close` it now — the fix isn't on `main` yet.
746	- **Cross-repo issue, or only partially resolved** — GitHub's closing keywords don't work across repos and shouldn't be used for partial work. Remember to leave a linking comment in Step 12b instead of closing it.
747	- **Ambiguous whether this PR fully resolves it** — this should already have been resolved in Step 2; if it wasn't, ask the user now rather than guessing at merge-closing behavior.
748	- Skip silently if no GitHub issue was identified in Step 2.
749	- Already authorized by the Step 8 "yes" — don't re-prompt.
750	
751	### Step 10: Rebase onto the latest base (last step before opening the PR)
752	
753	**This is the final step before the PR is opened.** Immediately before pushing, rebase the branch onto the freshest base so the PR opens against current `main` and merge conflicts surface here — locally, where they're cheap to resolve — instead of in GitHub's merge UI.
754	
755	This must happen **before** the first push (Step 11), not after. Rebasing a branch that's already on `origin` would require a force-push, which is forbidden without explicit user approval.
756	
757	```bash
758	git fetch origin
759	git rebase origin/main   # or the confirmed base branch from pre-flight
760	```
761	
762	- If the rebase is clean, proceed to Step 11.
763	- If the rebase hits conflicts, **stop and surface them to the user.** Resolve them (or have the user resolve them), then re-run Steps 4–5 (re-squash if needed, re-run `roborev review --wait`) so the review reflects the rebased history. Never `git rebase --skip` or abandon conflicting hunks silently.
764	- If the branch is already up to date with the base, the rebase is a no-op — proceed.
765	
766	### Step 11: Push the branch
767	
768	Once the rebase is clean, push the branch to `origin` with upstream tracking.
769	
770	```bash
771	git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
772	```
773	
774	Confirm the push succeeded before moving on. If it fails (auth, protected branch, non-fast-forward), surface the error and stop — do not force-push.
775	
776	### Step 12: Create the PR
777	
778	**Hard gate before running `gh pr create`: for every same-repo GitHub issue Step 2 determined this PR fully resolves, mechanically verify the drafted body contains a `Closes #NNN` / `Fixes #NNN` / `Resolves #NNN` line for *that specific* issue number before shelling out — one PR can fully resolve more than one issue, and each needs its own closing reference, not just the first.** This is a real known failure mode, not a hypothetical: gtm-sdk#609 was fully fixed by gtm-sdk#628, but the drafted body only listed "gtm-sdk#609" under Links without a closing keyword, so GitHub never auto-closed it and it sat open until manually closed later. A "the plan said to add it" belief is not sufficient — grep the actual string you're about to pass to `--body` for the pattern before running the command, once per fully-resolved issue number:
779	
780	```bash
781	grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY"
782	```
783	
784	`\b` is not portable to the BSD `grep` on macOS — use the `([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` form above instead, which matches the same "word boundary or end of string" intent on both BSD and GNU grep.
785	
786	If that grep fails for any fully-resolved issue number, **stop and fix the body** — don't proceed to `gh pr create` with a body that silently downgraded to a bare reference. If Step 2 flagged partial/cross-repo instead, the grep is expected to fail and that's correct — don't add the keyword in that case.
787	
788	To make this checkable, assign the HEREDOC to `PR_BODY` first, grep that exact variable, then pass it to `--body` — don't construct the body inline in the `gh pr create` call, since there's nothing to grep before shelling out:
789	
790	```bash
791	PR_BODY="$(cat <<'EOF'
792	## Why
793	... (real newlines, not \n)
794	EOF
795	)"
796	
797	for ISSUE_NUMBER in "${FULLY_RESOLVED_ISSUE_NUMBERS[@]}"; do  # every issue Step 2 flagged as fully resolved
798	  grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY" || {
799	    echo "missing closing keyword for #${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >&2
800	    exit 1
801	  }
802	done
803	
804	gh pr create --title "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup that double-charged credits" --body "$PR_BODY"
805	```
806	
807	Return the PR URL to the user. Don't add follow-up commentary unless the user asks — the URL is the work product.
808	
809	### Step 12b: Link the GitHub issue, if Step 9 deferred it
810	
811	Only applies when Step 9 flagged a **cross-repo or partially-resolved** issue — the fully-resolved same-repo case already carries its `Closes #NNN` in the PR body and needs no action here.
812	
813	```bash
814	gh issue comment <number> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>"                    # same-repo, partial
815	gh issue comment <number> --repo <owner/repo> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>" # cross-repo — use the owner/repo saved in Step 2
816	```
817	
818	- `<PR URL>` is the output from Step 12 — this step cannot run before Step 12 for exactly that reason.
819	- Do not close the issue yourself; partial or cross-repo work isn't the maintainer's signal to close it.
820	- Skip silently if Step 9 found nothing to do here.
821	
822	### Step 13: Suggest the merge once tests and checks pass
823	
824	Merging is never automatic. Once the PR is open, check its status with a single call (`gh pr checks <pr-number>`). When tests and required checks have passed, suggest merging with the GitHub CLI and wait for the user to say yes:
825	
826	```bash
827	gh pr merge <pr-number> --squash
828	```
829	
830	- Do not poll in a loop. If checks are still running, report that and stop; the user can ask again later.
831	- Do not log in to, configure, or call any merge-queue service. If `gh` is not authenticated, say so and stop.
832	- Never pass `--admin` or `--auto` unless the user asks for it.
833	
834	## Modifiers: drafts, reviewers, labels
835	
836	`gh pr create` accepts modifiers that don't affect the description but matter for the PR's lifecycle. Don't auto-set any of these; only pass what the user explicitly asks for:
837	
838	| Flag | When |
839	| --- | --- |
840	| `--draft` | User says "draft", or commit history shows clear in-progress markers ("WIP", "spike"). |
841	| `--reviewer <handle>` | Only when the user names reviewers. Don't guess. |
842	| `--label <name>` | Only labels that exist (`gh label list`). Invented labels silently no-op. |
843	| `--assignee <handle>` | Default to `@me` unless told otherwise. |
844	| `--base <branch>` | Only override the default branch when the user says so. |
845	
846	## Anti-patterns
847	
848	These show up in autogenerated PR descriptions and this skill must actively avoid them. Several come from defaults baked into other tools — including the default `gh pr create` template suggested by the Bash tool — and this skill overrides them.
849	
850	### Don't summarize the diff
851	
852	```markdown
853	## Summary
854	- Added `retry_with_backoff` helper in `apollo/client.py`
855	- Updated `enrich_account` to use it
856	- Added 3 unit tests in `test_apollo.py`
857	```
858	
859	The reviewer is about to read the diff. This is duplicate work that rots the moment the diff changes. Replace with **Why**.
860	
861	### Don't write empty sections
862	
863	```markdown
864	## Risks
865	None.
866	
867	## Test plan
868	Tested locally.
869	```
870	
871	"None" and "Tested locally" carry zero signal. Drop the section.
872	
873	### Don't add AI attribution
874	
875	The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) prohibit AI attribution in commits and PRs.
876	**Never** emit:
877	
878	- `Co-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>`
879	- `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](...)`
880	- Any "Generated by ..." or "Powered by ..." footer
881	
882	The Bash tool's default PR template includes the 🤖 footer. **Strip it.** This skill overrides that default.
883	
884	### Don't restate the title
885	
886	If the title is "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup", the description shouldn't open with "This PR fixes a race in the Apollo enrichment dedup logic." Start the Why with the problem, not a rephrase.
887	
888	### Don't pad with boilerplate
889	
890	- "This PR makes some improvements to ..."
891	- "As discussed offline, ..."
892	- "Cleaning up some technical debt ..."
893	
894	If you can't write a specific Why, pause and ask the user. Vague motivation is a tell that the work isn't ready for review.
895	
896	### Don't paste test output
897	
898	The Test plan section is about the *reasoning* behind what was tested. A reviewer can run the tests. They cannot rederive your reasoning from the output.
899	
900	### Don't include "Closes #NNN" without confirming
901	
902	GitHub auto-closes referenced issues on merge. Only use `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves` keywords if Step 2 confirmed the PR fully resolves a **same-repo** issue. For partial work or a cross-repo issue, mention it in Links instead and leave a linking comment on the issue in Step 12b — no magic keyword. Skipping the confirmation in Step 2 is a bug, not a safe default: it leaves the issue open with no trace back to the PR that addressed it.
903	
904	### Don't autopilot the PR submission
905	
906	Even if the user said "create a PR for this", they agreed to the action, not to a specific draft. Show the draft, wait for confirmation, then submit.
907	
908	## Examples
909	
910	### Example 1: Small bug fix — Why + Links only
911	
912	**Title:** `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts`
913	
914	**Body:**
915	
916	```markdown
917	## Why
918	The Apollo `search_people` paginator was dropping the last page of results because the cursor check used `>` instead of `>=`. Affected every batch where total results were an exact multiple of page_size — roughly 10% of runs. Caught when a TAM build was missing ~50 known contacts ([AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)).
919	
920	## Links
921	- Linear: [AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)
922	```
923	
924	(Trade-offs, Risks, Test plan dropped — small obvious fix, full coverage exists.)
925	
926	### Example 2: Refactor — Why + Trade-offs + Risks + Links
927	
928	**Title:** `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear → Attio sync`
929	
930	**Body:**
931	
932	```markdown
933	## Why
934	Five call sites in `libs/attio/` were duplicating retry/backoff logic, and each had drifted: `update_person` retried on 5xx but not 429; `create_person` retried on 429 but with no backoff; `list_workspaces` did no retry at all. The new Linear → Attio sync was about to become the sixth divergent copy.
935	
936	Pulling the logic into `@retry_with_backoff` lets callers opt in with one line and ensures consistent behavior across all Attio writes.
937	
938	## Trade-offs
939	Considered `tenacity` instead. Rejected because the call sites already have idiosyncratic logic — custom backoff that respects Attio's `Retry-After` header — that `tenacity` would require a custom wait strategy to express. The hand-rolled decorator is ~30 lines and stays close to the Attio-specific behavior.
940	
941	## Risks
942	Changes the *shape* of exceptions that bubble up: `AttioRateLimit` is now wrapped in `RetryExhausted` after N attempts. Two existing callers caught `AttioRateLimit` directly; both updated in this PR. Grep for `AttioRateLimit` returns no other matches.
943	
944	## Links
945	- Linear: [AI-2891](https://linear.app/...)
946	- Spec: design/backlog-202604010000-attio_retry_decorator-spec-01.md
947	```
948	
949	### Example 3: Bad → Good
950	
951	**Bad:**
952	
953	```markdown
954	## Summary
955	- Added retry decorator
956	- Updated 5 Attio call sites
957	- Removed duplicate retry code
958	- Added tests
959	
960	## Test plan
961	- [x] Ran tests
962	- [x] Tested locally
963	
964	🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
965	```
966	
967	What's wrong: the Summary paraphrases the diff, the Test plan has no reasoning, the AI footer is forbidden, and there's no motivation a reviewer can use to evaluate the change.
968	
969	**Good:** see Example 2.
970	
971	## Failure modes and recovery
972	
973	| What happened | What to do |
974	| --- | --- |
975	| Linear MCP unavailable or ticket not found | Continue without the Linear context. Note in Links: "Linear ticket: AI-NNN (MCP unavailable at draft time)" and let the user fill in. |
976	| Branch doesn't match a Linear pattern | Skip the Linear lookup. Rely on design artifacts and conversation. |
977	| No design artifact, no ticket, no clear Why from the conversation | Stop. Ask the user: "I can't establish a specific Why for this PR from the available context. Can you summarize the motivation in 1-2 sentences?" |
978	| `gh pr create` fails (auth, network, no remote) | Surface the error to the user. Don't retry without diagnosing. |
979	| User rejects the draft | Take their feedback and rewrite. Don't argue. |
980	| User wants to skip the confirmation step | Honor it — but require an explicit "skip confirmation" or "just create it" from them. Default is to confirm. |
981	
982	## Common pitfalls
983	
984	| Pitfall | Why it bites | Fix |
985	| --- | --- | --- |
986	| Drafting before pre-flight checks | PR opened against stale base, with uncommitted work left behind | Run the pre-flight batch first |
987	| Not checking for an existing PR | Duplicate PR, or `gh pr create` errors out | Always `gh pr view` first |
988	| Pasting the Linear ticket verbatim | Description becomes a wall of duplicated text | Paraphrase the problem statement; link the rest |
989	| Filling all sections regardless of signal | Skim-defeating filler | Drop sections that don't carry meaning |
990	| Autopiloting `gh pr create` | Premature publication; harder to retract than to delay | Show draft, wait for confirmation |
991	| Inheriting the default 🤖 footer | Violates the repo's no-AI-attribution rule | Strip it from the body |
992	| Trusting a clean roborev as proof the code runs | Roborev reviews the diff, not test execution — a hardcoded test assertion (e.g. a literal YAML `if:` string) can still fail in CI | Run the mirrored test file / grep for affected literals before roborev (Step 5) |
993	| Using "WIP" in title instead of `--draft` | Title noise; doesn't actually mark the PR as draft | Use `gh pr create --draft` and a clean title |
994	| Linking to the PR's own branch name as "context" | The branch is implicit; this is noise | Only link to artifacts that aren't already obvious from the PR |
995	| Forgetting the linked GitHub issue entirely | Issue lingers open after merge with no trace back to the PR that fixed it | Resolve it in Step 2, `Closes #NNN` in Step 7, record disposition in Step 9, comment in Step 12b |
996	| Drafting `Closes #NNN` in Step 7 but the final body sent to `gh pr create` drops it (edits, re-drafts, template drift) | Issue never auto-closes even though Step 2/9 correctly flagged full resolution — happened for real on gtm-sdk#609/#628 | Step 12's mechanical grep gate on the literal `--body` string, not on what Step 7 intended to write |
997	
998	## Red flags (stop and rethink)
999	
1000	- **About to `git push` without running `roborev review --wait` first.** This is the repository-wide roborev gate defined in the repo's agent instructions; no PR should skip it.
1001	- **About to `git push` with more commits than the PR needs.** Squash to a coherent set first (Step 4); don't rely on GitHub's "Squash and merge" button to clean up history before review.
1002	- Drafting a PR with no Linear ticket, no design artifact, and no conversation-derived motivation.
1003	- Writing more than 3 paragraphs in Why. If you need that much, the work is probably two PRs.
1004	- Including a `## Summary` section. This is the default template's tell — replace with `## Why`.
1005	- Including a 🤖 footer.
1006	- More than 5 bullets in any one section. Each bullet should be load-bearing.
1007	- A title that ends in a period, or starts with "Update", "Fix some", "Misc", "Various".
1008	- A title that uses a Conventional Commits prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). PR titles are formal sentences, not commit subjects.
1009	- A title that describes *what* the diff does (e.g., "Add X helper", "Refactor Y module") when a *why* framing was available.

- Use `gh pr create --base main` to create a PR onto the target branch. Keep the title under 80 characters. Keep the description under five sentences, unless the user instructed you otherwise. Describe not just changes made in this session but ALL changes in the workspace diff.

<!-- Canonical source: flox-conductor-sandbox prompts/conductor/create-pr.md.
     Installed into a repo's .conductor settings [prompts].create_pr by
     scripts/install-conductor-prompts.py — do not hand-edit the TOML copy.
     Upstream history: gtm-sdk prompts/conductor/create-pr.md (incl. #921).
